new_targets.why: Dify (155,674★, 24k forks) is the dominant self-hosted LLM application and agentic workflow platform — MCP support, agent nodes, RAG pipelines, skills, and a workflow canvas used by tens of thousands of teams. It is the highest-star non-n8n target ever identified in this scan. Tool/skill invocations in the agent pipeline fire after LLM decision with no per-agent identity binding — any tool call executes under the operator credential regardless of which model or sub-agent triggered it. Bolyra's EVC verifier, wired in as an optional pre-tool hook or a Dify plugin credential type, adds identity binding at the widest possible deployment footprint.
new_targets.gap: Dify's tool node execution pipeline (api/core/tools/tool_engine.py and api/core/workflow/nodes/tool/) dispatches tools after parsing LLM output with no caller-identity check. An optional BolyraAuthProvider credential type — registered in api/core/tools/provider/ — and a one-line pre_tool_invoke() hook closes the gap without changing existing workflows. Non-breaking: tools without the credential run exactly as today.
new_targets.anchor_issue: Search langgenius/dify issues for 'authorization', 'tool guard', 'per-agent permission', or 'identity'. At 1,043 open issues, demand for access control on agent tool calls is highly likely. The repo has CONTRIBUTING.md and a very active maintainer community (updated today, 2026-09-14).
new_targets.pr_type: targeted feature — BolyraAuthProvider credential type + optional pre_tool_invoke() hook in the tool engine. 2-3 files. Ships as an optional provider; existing deployments unaffected. A companion example Dify workflow template demonstrates the integration.
new_targets.builder_notes: Entry points: api/core/tools/provider/ for the credential type, api/core/tools/tool_engine.py for the hook. Dify uses Python 3.11+, ruff, mypy. Run make lint before submitting. Tests in api/tests/. The Dify team reviews external contribs within days for scoped, well-documented PRs. The MCP integration in Dify makes Bolyra's EVC verifier doubly compelling — it can gate both native tools and MCP tools in the same hook.

new_targets.why: browser-use (114,572★, 12.5k forks) is the dominant open-source browser-automation agent framework — Playwright-based, Python, integrates with every major LLM. Agents dispatch browser actions (click, fill, navigate, extract) after LLM instruction with no identity gate; any code that instantiates an Agent has full browser access. Browser actions are uniquely high-risk: they can transact, sign forms, exfiltrate data, and perform OAuth flows — precisely the action class that Bolyra's mandate model was designed to gate. An optional pre_action callback on the Agent object is the cleanest injection point, verified before each browser action the LLM dispatches.
new_targets.gap: browser-use's Agent.step() (browser_use/agent/service.py) iterates LLM instructions and dispatches browser actions directly. There is no pre-dispatch hook for identity or mandate verification. An optional authorization_callback parameter on Agent — evaluated before each action — closes the gap. Fallback: if absent, behavior is identical to today. A BolyraAuthCallback helper in a contrib/bolyra/ directory provides the ready-to-use EVC check.
new_targets.anchor_issue: Search browser-use/browser-use issues for 'authorization', 'permission', 'access control', or 'identity'. At 408 open issues and active community engagement, demand for per-session or per-action authorization is almost certain. The framework is actively maintained (updated 2026-09-14).
new_targets.pr_type: targeted feature — optional authorization_callback parameter on Agent class + BolyraAuthCallback contrib example. 2 files: browser_use/agent/service.py (add optional callback), contrib/bolyra/auth_callback.py (EVC check helper). Non-breaking.
new_targets.builder_notes: Entry point: browser_use/agent/service.py — study the step() loop and ActionModel types. browser-use uses uv, Python 3.11+, ruff. Run uv run pytest before submitting. The project has an active Discord and contributor community; filing an issue first ('add optional pre-action authorization hook') reduces PR merge risk. The Playwright integration means Bolyra can gate the highest-risk browser actions (form submission, payment flows) specifically, which is a compelling demo angle.

new_targets.why: UI-TARS-desktop (38,971★) is ByteDance's open-source multimodal AI agent stack for computer-use, GUI automation, and browser-use — it integrates MCP servers, coordinates agent-TARS workflows, and dispatches tool/GUI actions through a GUI operator pipeline. Computer-use actions (clicking, typing, form submission, application control) are the highest-risk agent action class, yet the dispatch pipeline has no per-session identity gate. Bolyra's EVC verifier as a pre-dispatch hook in the agent-TARS tool pipeline closes the gap for the entire computer-use tier of agents — a first for this space.
new_targets.gap: UI-TARS-desktop's action dispatch pipeline (apps/agent-tars/src/main/agent/ or the tool dispatcher) dispatches LLM-selected GUI/browser actions with no identity verification. An optional BolyraAuthMiddleware in the MCP tool dispatch path — or as a named authorization plugin in the agent pipeline — gates each action before execution. Non-breaking: absent the plugin, behavior is unchanged.
new_targets.anchor_issue: Search bytedance/UI-TARS-desktop issues for 'authorization', 'permission', 'access control', or 'identity'. At 444 open issues there is likely demand for session-level authorization on high-risk GUI actions. ByteDance's agent stack positions for enterprise — where identity binding matters most.
new_targets.pr_type: targeted contrib — BolyraAuthMiddleware plugin in a plugins/bolyra/ directory, wired into the MCP tool dispatch path. TypeScript strict, follows existing plugin patterns in the repo. Companion example showing a delegation-constrained UI-TARS session.
new_targets.builder_notes: Entry point: study the agent-TARS application structure (apps/agent-tars/) and the MCP integration (packages/agent-infra/mcp-server/). new_targets.why: LibreChat (43,384★, 9k forks) is the most-deployed self-hosted ChatGPT clone — Agents, MCP, Skills, multi-model, secure multi-user auth, Code Interpreter, OpenAPI Actions. It has an existing auth system for users, but agent tool/MCP dispatch runs without per-agent identity binding: any agent with a session key can call any registered tool or MCP server at full operator permission. Bolyra's EVC verifier as a pre-tool hook in the agent middleware closes the gap between user-auth (what LibreChat already has) and action-auth (what it is missing). The active user+developer community makes a well-scoped PR high-visibility.
new_targets.gap: LibreChat's agent tool dispatch (api/server/services/Endpoints/ or the MCP middleware in api/server/middleware/) runs tools after LLM selection with no per-action mandate check. An optional BolyraAuthMiddleware in the Express middleware chain — evaluated before each MCP or tool invocation — adds per-action identity binding. The integration point is clean: LibreChat already has middleware layers for auth and rate-limiting; adding Bolyra as an optional middleware is a natural fit.
new_targets.anchor_issue: Search danny-avila/LibreChat issues for 'tool authorization', 'MCP permission', 'per-agent access control', or 'action identity'. At 731 open issues there is almost certainly demand from enterprise self-hosters for fine-grained tool permissions. LibreChat is actively maintained (updated 2026-09-14).
new_targets.pr_type: targeted feature — optional BolyraAuthMiddleware in api/server/middleware/ + configuration flag in librechat.yaml. Non-breaking: disabled by default. TypeScript strict, follows existing Express middleware patterns.
new_targets.builder_notes: Entry point: study api/server/middleware/ and the MCP integration in api/server/services/. LibreChat uses pnpm, TypeScript strict. Run npm run test:api before submitting. The multi-user deployment model means Bolyra can bind each user's agent session to a distinct mandate — a stronger story than single-key deployments. CONTRIBUTING.md exists and maintainer is responsive to quality external contributions.

new_targets.why: AgentOps (5,817★) is the dominant Python SDK for AI agent monitoring — it integrates with CrewAI, OpenAI Agents SDK, Langchain, Autogen, AG2, and CamelAI through a single decorator/init pattern. Because AgentOps sits in the observability layer across all these frameworks, it is the single highest-leverage integration point for adding identity-bound authorization observability to the entire Python agent ecosystem. A BolyraSessionDecorator that attaches a Bolyra mandate to each AgentOps session — emitting identity-verified action events alongside the existing cost/latency events — turns Bolyra's proof into a first-class audit signal across every framework AgentOps monitors.
new_targets.gap: AgentOps's action event pipeline (agentops/event.py, agentops/session.py) records tool calls, LLM calls, and action events, but has no concept of a caller identity or mandate binding. An optional bolyra_mandate field on BolyraSession (wrapping agentops.start_session()) and a pre-event hook that emits an EVC verdict alongside each action event closes the gap. Any team using AgentOps gets Bolyra's authorization audit trail as an opt-in column in their existing AgentOps dashboard.
new_targets.anchor_issue: Search AgentOps-AI/agentops issues for 'authorization', 'identity', 'mandate', or 'access control'. The observability angle — 'prove which agent was authorized to take which action' — aligns with enterprise compliance requirements that AgentOps customers already face.
new_targets.pr_type: contrib integration — optional BolyraSessionDecorator in agentops/integrations/bolyra/ (follows existing integration pattern for crewai/, openai/, etc.) plus optional bolyra_mandate field on Session. Zero change to core event pipeline. Python 3.10+.
new_targets.builder_notes: Study an existing AgentOps integration (agentops/integrations/crewai/ or agentops/integrations/openai/) to learn the integration pattern. Python, uses ruff + pytest. CONTRIBUTING.md exists. The AgentOps maintainers are responsive to integrations that expand the framework coverage — Bolyra is in good company with the existing CrewAI, OpenAI Agents, and AG2 integrations already shipped.
